blocks.text: It happens all the time, says Kholoud al-Ameri, an Iraqi journalist and the editor of a news website. “Female journalists here are often getting messages, and mostly from men,” she explains. “They somehow find you online and then they say they just want to talk or they want to add you on Instagram or Facebook,” says al-Ameri, who also heads a network of female journalists working on climate change stories. “Sometimes it’s hard because the men say they’re our readers and we don’t want to discourage them.
